chunks: Rijal al-Kashshi: Hamduwayh and Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Ziyad ibn Abi al-Hilal who said:

Our companions differed regarding the narrations of Jabir al-Ju'fi, so I said to them: I will ask Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him). When I entered, he began by saying: May Allah have mercy on Jabir al-Ju'fi, he used to tell the truth about us; may Allah curse al-Mughira ibn Sa'id, he used to lie about us.

key_terms.الْمُغِيرَةُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ: Al-Mughira ibn Sa'id, a companion often contrasted with Jabir for his reliability
key_terms.جَابِرٌ الْجَعْفِيُّ: Jabir al-Ju'fi, a prominent companion of the Imams known for his extensive narrations
key_terms.يَكْذِبُ عَلَيْنَا: He used to lie about us (the Imams)
key_terms.يُصَدِّقُ عَلَيْنَا: He used to tell the truth about us (the Imams)

ai.seo_question: How did Imam al-Sadiq distinguish between truthful and lying narrators like Jabir al-Ju'fi and al-Mughira ibn Sa'id?
ai.summary: This narration from Rijal al-Kashshi illustrates the early scholarly debate regarding the reliability of Jabir al-Ju'fi, a prominent narrator of the Imams. Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) resolves this discrepancy by affirming Jabir's truthfulness ('was truthful to us') while contrasting him with al-Mughira ibn Sa'id, who was known for fabricating hadiths, thereby establishing a clear criterion for distinguishing between authentic and weak narrators in Shia tradition.

en.ammaar-muslim: 2. [2/136] Rijal al-Kashshi: Hamduwayh and Ibrahim from Muhammad b. Isa from Ali b. al-Hakam from Ziyad b. Abi al-Hilal who said:

our companions differed about accepting the narrations of Jabir al-Ju`fi, I said to them: I will ask Aba Abdillah عليه السلام, so when I entered upon him, he عليه السلام began saying [without me asking]: may Allah have mercy on Jabir al-Ju`fi – he used, to tell the truth about us, may Allah curse al-Mughira bin Sa`id, he used to lie about us.
